jobs.title: Senior Advisor, Strategic Planning
jobs.description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become a Senior Advisor, Strategic Planning at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you’ll be responsible for leading key components of the annual strategic planning process, helping shape how an electric utility serving about 15 million people navigates a period of rapid growth and transformation. In this highly visible role, you will be driving enterprise strategic initiatives from ideation to implementation with partners across SCE’s business areas and will be responsible for preparing the analysis and materials for these topics for Board-level corporate strategy discussions. You will tackle complex questions at the intersection of clean energy, affordability, reliability, resilience, technology and public policy.

As a Senior Advisor, Strategic Planning , your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

Responsibilities

- Performs scenario analysis and enhanced analytics to assist management in understanding the economic impacts of business decisions.
- Identifies and develops innovative cost savings projects and initiatives related to energy infrastructure and supply.
- Ensures that the financial modelling and sales forecasts are aligned with market and maintain reasonable margins.
- Formulates strategies alongside the business development team to diversify in new complementary markets and products.
- Develops and continuously optimizes the organizational structure and efficient business processes. Undertakes strategic analysis of markets and competition, developing conceptual frameworks and conducting qualitative and quantitative analyses to identify new growth opportunities.
- Analyzes and engages with strategic acquisition targets and works with the appropriate stakeholders to evaluate fit and strategic merit.
- Leverages insights to support strategic recommendations for the company, with guidance from project leads. Leads financing and risk assessment efforts for growth opportunities covering joint ventures and acquisitions for energy infrastructure projects.
- Leads analysis, valuation, diligence, and integration for all transactions.
- A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

- Five or more years of experience in strategy and/or management consulting, venture capital, investment banking, or corporate strategy.

Preferred Qualifications

- Demonstrated experience driving strategic initiatives through implementation within large and complex organizations.
- Understanding of the unique business and regulatory model of investor-owned utilities.
- Willingness to challenge traditional approaches and assumptions to provide fresh strategic perspectives.
- Demonstrated growth mindset, intellectual curiosity, and commitment to continuous learning.
- Motivated by creating lasting organizational impact and advancing strategic priorities that benefit the broader enterprise.
- MBA or similar graduate-level education.

Additional Information

- This position’s work mode is hybrid. The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California.  Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The work mode can be changed based on business needs.
- Visit our Candidate Resource page to get meaningful information related to benefits, perks, resources, testing information, hiring process, and more!
- The primary work location for this position is Rosemead, CA.
- Relocation may apply to this position.

jobs.title: Enterprise Cybersecurity Senior Advisor- AI Strategy
jobs.description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become an Enterprise Cybersecurity Senior Advisor at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you’ll serve as a senior technical and strategic leader responsible for defining, maintaining, and socializing SCE Cybersecurity’s AI strategy and roadmap. This role will translate enterprise objectives, emerging AI capabilities, threat trends, regulatory expectations, and Cybersecurity operating needs into a coherent AI cybersecurity strategy that enables responsible innovation, measurable risk reduction, and operational resilience across SCE.

More specifically, you’ll:
- Own and continuously refine the multi-year Cybersecurity AI strategy, priorities, guiding principles, and measurable outcomes.
- Maintain an integrated technical roadmap for AI-enabled cyber defense, secure enterprise AI adoption, and AI risk reduction.
- Assess emerging AI technologies, threat trends, regulatory developments, and industry practices to identify risks, opportunities, and recommended actions for SCE.
- Define cybersecurity requirements, reference patterns, guardrails, and control expectations for AI platforms, solutions, data, models, and third-party services.
- Lead cybersecurity participation in AI strategy planning across the enterprise, perform architecture reviews, investment planning, and technology-selection decisions.
- Partner across Cybersecurity, IT, data, privacy, legal, compliance, risk, procurement, operations, and business teams to integrate security throughout the AI lifecycle.
- Develop executive briefings, dashboards, decision papers, and roadmap updates that clearly communicate progress, risk, tradeoffs, dependencies, and funding needs.
- Establish success measures and governance rhythms to track roadmap execution, control effectiveness, risk reduction, and realized business value.
- Advise leaders on responsible AI adoption, including appropriate human oversight, monitoring, resilience, incident response, and regulatory considerations.
- Provide thought leadership, mentoring, and practical guidance that builds organizational understanding of AI-related cybersecurity risks and capabilities.

As an Enterprise Cybersecurity Senior Advisor , your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

Responsibilities

- Drives endpoint security across the organization, ensuring that Enterprise and Platform infrastructure is secure, protecting SCE's employees and customers.
- Participates in determination of security requirements, evaluates business strategies and requirements, researches information security standards, conducts system security and vulnerability analyses and risk assessments, studies architecture and platform; identifies integration issues; and prepares cost estimates.
- Facilitates planning security systems by evaluating network and security technologies, develops requirements for local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), virtual private networks (VPNs), routers, firewalls, and related security and network devices, and designs public key infrastructures (PKIs) adhering to industry standards.
- Leads implementation of security systems by specifying intrusion detection methodologies and equipment; directs equipment and software installation and calibration; prepares preventive and reactive measures; creating, transmitting, and maintaining keys; provides technical support; completes documentation.
- Monitors and ensures compliance to standards, policies, and procedures by conducting incident response analyses and participating in training programs.
- Prepares system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends.
- Performs risk assessments and threat modeling exercises to identify risks in home-grown and third-party services and applications.
- Creates security tooling to secure corporate infrastructure and development environments. Documents processes for and provides support of the Enterprise Security Architecture.
- Provides guidance on the data security processes, including encryption, privacy management, data classification and assigning certain security levels based on classification.
- A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

- Ten or more years of experience in information technology, information security and/or cybersecurity.
- US Citizenship Required.

Preferred Qualifications
- Ten or more years of experience in enterprise architecture, AI strategy, security strategy, or related technology strategy functions.
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or related discipline.
- Experience developing enterprise strategies, technical roadmaps, capability models, program plans, or investment recommendations for complex technology environments.
- Experience translating technical cybersecurity topics into executive-ready communications, including briefings, roadmaps, decision papers, metrics, and risk-based recommendations.
- Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, governance models, risk management practices, architecture practices, and security controls applicable to enterprise and critical infrastructure environments.
- Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes across teams without direct authority, work independently on ambiguous assignments, and establish objectives, plans, and deliverables with broad organizational impact.
- Experience developing or governing AI, GenAI, machine learning, agentic AI, AI security, AI risk management, or AI-enabled cybersecurity capabilities.
- Experience with AI security concepts such as model/prompt/data security, AI threat modeling, adversarial testing, privacy and data protection, logging and monitoring, human oversight, and secure AI lifecycle controls.
- Experience aligning cybersecurity requirements with enterprise AI platforms, AI Centers of Excellence, data governance, cloud platforms, identity controls, cyber operations, or DevSecOps processes.
- Experience in utility, critical infrastructure, operational technology, regulated, or large enterprise environments.
- Familiarity with relevant frameworks and standards such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-82, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS, Zero Trust, SABSA, TOGAF, IEC 62443, or related industry practices.
- One or more relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, GSEC, cloud security, AI/ML security, architecture, or related certifications.

Additional Information

Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become a Senior Advisor, Continuous Improvement at Southern California Edison (SCE) and and play a critical role in transforming how Customer Service improves performance and delivers results. In this highly impactful role, you will lead the deployment of Customer Service's continuous improvement framework, partnering with leaders to identify performance gaps, solve complex operational challenges, and implement sustainable improvements. You will leverage performance metrics, operational insights, and structured problem-solving methodologies to drive accountability, improve customer outcomes, and enable Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Performance Reviews to serve as catalysts for continuous improvement across the organization. Join a team dedicated to operational excellence, continuous improvement, and delivering exceptional customer experiences while helping build a cleaner energy future.

Incident Management Team Expected Participation : Employees are expected to support emergency response and/or business continuity efforts, including readiness to serve on an Incident Management Team (IMT) when needed. Employees will participate in an on-call rotation (approximately every four to six weeks), to support IMT activations during emergency events. IMT assignments may differ from an individual’s regular responsibilities.

As a   Senior Advisor, Continuous Improvement , your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

- Conducts analyses and oversees the preparation of reports that provide operational and technical support to business operations.
- Designs and implements key performance indicators (KPIs) to streamline business strategy and leads key process improvement initiatives that help achieve company goals and improve customer satisfaction.
- A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

- Ten or more years of experience in business process improvement or operational excellence initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience applying Lean Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies within large-scale customer service or operational environments.
- Experience implementing continuous improvement or operational excellence programs and driving sustainable process improvements.
- Experience using performance metrics, KPIs, and management review processes to identify improvement opportunities, drive accountability, and sustain results.
- Experience facilitating root-cause analysis, problem-solving workshops, Kaizen events, or leader-led improvement activities.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, facilitation, change management, and communication skills.
